Senses.PreferredTarget: follow the waves and ride the swells
Senses.Note: Seven exact witnesses in seven independent works support one wave-following image with positive and critical stances; the stance changes, not the lexical object.

Occurrences.Kwic: 有時一句。隨波逐浪。若也途中受用。遇知音別機宜。識休咎相共證明。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Blue Cliff Record of Chan Master Foguo Yuanwu (佛果圜悟禪師碧巖錄): Yuanwu Keqin says a phrase may follow the waves on the road, meeting a knowing companion and distinguishing the occasion.

Occurrences.Kwic: 若隨波逐浪去。種種建立觸處圓融。若截斷眾流去。把住要津不通凡聖。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Foguo Yuanwu (圓悟佛果禪師語錄): Yuanwu Keqin contrasts wave-following responsiveness with stream-cutting closure.

Occurrences.Kwic: 雲門優穩身心。自解隨波逐浪。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Extensive Record of Chan Master Hongzhi (宏智禪師廣錄): Hongzhi Zhengjue says Yunmen Wenyan, steady in body and mind, knew how to follow the waves.

Occurrences.Kwic: 隨波逐浪趁風遊，月下垂鉤放小舟，識得句中消息子，回頭不住在中流。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Recorded Sayings of Tianyin (天隱和尚語錄): Tianyin Yuanxiu's verse follows waves and wind in a small boat but turns back rather than remaining midstream.

Occurrences.Kwic: 即此一喝問事荅事，問理荅理，謂之隨波逐浪句。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Ruibai Mingxue (入就瑞白禪師語錄): Ruibai Mingxue calls a shout that answers affair with affair and principle with principle the wave-following phrase.

Occurrences.Kwic: 者僧用揀擇心隨波逐浪，當陽不薦，覿面蹉過。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Feiyin (費隱禪師語錄): Feiyin Tongrong criticizes the monastic in the Zhaozhou cypress case for following the waves with a discriminating mind and missing what is directly present.
Teaching Collection of Chan Master Shiyu (石雨禪師法檀): Shiyu Mingfang says Yunmen only managed to follow the waves in his judgment of the Qianfeng case.

Senses.Explanation: Records use this phrase for moving responsively with the occasion, but Feiyin Tongrong turns it into criticism when the historical monastic in Zhaozhou's cypress case drifts with discriminating thought. The image is “follow the waves and ride the swells,” one member of the Yunmen three-phrase frame. In the Blue Cliff Record, Yuanwu Keqin says a phrase can follow the waves when used on the road, meeting a knowing companion and distinguishing what the occasion calls for. His recorded sayings contrast going with the waves, where varied establishments are responsive at every point, with cutting off all streams and barring ordinary and sage. Hongzhi Zhengjue says Yunmen, steady in body and mind, knew how to follow the waves. Tianyin Yuanxiu's verse follows waves and wind in a small boat but turns back rather than remaining midstream. Ruibai Mingxue defines the phrase-function through a shout that answers an affair with the affair and principle with principle. Feiyin Tongrong, by contrast, criticizes a monastic whose discriminating mind follows the waves and misses what is directly present; Shiyu Mingfang similarly says Yunmen “only managed” to follow the waves in a disputed case.
